AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Ivan Altamirano called meeting to order at 5:12 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any Closed Session items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The City Council recessed to Closed Session at 5:13 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION The City Council reconvened to open session at 6:08 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Noel Tapia reported on Closed Session Items No. 1 and 2, stating that with the entire Council present, two potential litigation matters and Item No. 2 were discussed. Staff provided a presentation, the City Council gave direction, and no reportable action was taken for any items.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Ivan Altamirano called the regular City Council meeting to order at 6:09 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Public Works Director Shahid Abbas led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Mayor Pro Tem Kevin Lainez offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation - National Breast Cancer Awareness Month in the City of Commerce Social Services Coordinator Moyra Garcia provided a brief presentation on the item. Mayor Ivan Altamirano then read the proclamation. 

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoyotl spoke regarding arts in public places subcommittee. Mayor Ivan Altamirano followed up by discussing future programs where seniors can take art classes and contribute art to the City.




CONSENT CALENDAR

4.. Granting Authority for Execution of Metro, State, and Federally Funded Grants, Documents for City Projects Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 25-64 authorizing the City Manager, Public Works Director, or his designee to sign all documents related to Metro, State, and Federally funded grants for Capital Improvement Projects. 

9.. Residential Parking T Markings Pilot Program  -  Action: withdraw

14.. Introduction and First reading of Ordinance No. 824 Enacting Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment No. 25-02 Amending Title 19, Chapter 19.25 of the Commerce Municipal Code (Signs) Modifying Existing Billboard Regulations and Adding City-Wide Digital Billboard Regulations - Public Hearing  -  Action: approve the proposed ordinance on first reading (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally opened the public hearing at 7:28 p.m. 
There we no individuals wishing to address the City Council for this item. 
Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally closed the public hearing at 7:28 p.m.

Scott Sheldon from Scott Realty Advisors provided a presentation on the ordinance. 

5.. Gateway Water Management Authority Appointments Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 25-65 continuing the City’s participation in the Gateway Water Management Authority as an active Board member and adopt the Resolution appointing Shahid Abbas, Director of Public Works as the Governing Board Member and Andrew Caraveo, Environmental Coordinator as the designated alternate representative.

15.. Introduction and First reading of Ordinance No. 825 Enacting Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment No. 25-04 Amending Title 19 (Zoning) of the Commerce Municipal Code (“CMC”) to Allow Entertainment Establishments in Certain Manufacturing Zones, Create Parking Requirements for this Use, and Revise the Definition for Entertainment Establishments - Public Hearing  -  Action: approve the proposed ordinance on first reading (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Community Services Director Jessica Serrano provided a presentation on the ordinance.

Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally opened the public hearing at 7:50 p.m. 
There we no individuals wishing to address the City Council for this item. 
Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally closed the public hearing at 7:50 p.m.


2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 5A, 5B, 5C, and 5A S/A Action Taken: The City Council and Successor Agency approved the bills and claims set forth in Warrant Registers No. 5A dated October 14, 2025, 5B for the period of September 18, 2025 through September 22, 2025, 5C for the period of September 24, 2025 through October 7, 2025, and 5A S/A for the period of September 25, 2025 through October 2, 2025.

3.. Approval of Minutes Action Taken: The City Council and Successor Agency approved the minutes of the  City Council meeting of Tuesday, September 23, 2025, held at 5:00 p.m. and the minutes of the Special City Council meeting of Tuesday, October 7, 2025, held at 5:00 p.m.

6.. Eligibility Expansion for Competitive Sports Programs  -  Action: withdraw

11.. Arts in Public Places Program: Art Installation at 5281 E. Washington Blvd.  -  Action: approve as amended (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia Ernie Hernandez presented the item. Mayor Altamirano provided additional comments.

12.. Arts in Public Places Program: Art Installation at 5650 Jillson Street  -  Action: continue Mayor Altamirano presented the item.

10.. Arts in Public Places Program: Installation of Nine (9) Utility Box Murals and one (1) Post Office Box Mural  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia City Manager Ernie Hernandez presented. Mayor Altamirano made additional comments.

Staff will research local scholars, athletes, and artists from Commerce to celebrate on the remaining utility boxes and use a variety of local artists. The option to create art wraps will also be explored. Staff will determine if there is an option to use two (2) art pieces on either side of one (1) utility box.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Barreras provided a statistics update for the dates of 9/1/25-9/30/25.

PUBLIC HEARING

13.. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Title 19 (Zoning) of the Commerce Municipal Code to Establish Artificial Turf Regulations for All Zones Citywide and in the Public Right-of-way - Public Hearing  -  Action: continue (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Community Services Director Jessica Serrano provided a presentation on the Ordinance. 

The Council provided further direction to City Staff requesting more information regarding the City's liability.

Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally opened the public hearing at 7:27 p.m. 
There we no individuals wishing to address the City Council for this item at this time.


CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Mireya Garcia - Thanked her colleagues, Mayor Altamirano, staff, and Anthony Aguilar for their support in creating the Purple Heart City Plaque to honor the men and women who have been wounded or killed in action by enemy forces, and thanked them for keeping us safe. The plaque will be presented to them on Veteran's Day, November 11th. 

Councilmember Oralia Y. Rebollo - Thanked the Parks & Recreation Department and Camp Commerce staff for the Women's Getaway Weekend. 

Councilmember Hugo A. Argumedo - No Reports

Mayor Pro Tem Kevin Lainez - Thanked the Citadel Outlets staff for the Citadel Clean Up Commerce Event and for their contributions to youth organizations that participated. Thanked the Commerce Boys & Girls Water Polo Programs, Unplugged Performing Arts, and Commerce Crush for their participation. He also thanked the Parks and Recreation and Transportation Department for the LAFC Community Night.

Mayor Ivan Altamirano - No Reports

ADJOURNMENT The meeting adjourned at 8:02 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

16.. Resolution No. 25-67 Amending User (“Planning”) Fees For Planning Permits and Approvals Pursuant to Title 19 (“Zoning”) of the City of Commerce Municipal Code  - Public Hearing  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Community Services Director Jessica Serrano provided a presentation on the resolution.

Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally opened the public hearing at 7:57 p.m. 
There we no individuals wishing to address the City Council for this item. 
Mayor Ivan Altamirano formally closed the public hearing at 7:57 p.m.


7.. New Transit Maintenance Facility Project  -  Action: adopt Moved by Kevin Lainez

Approval of the Consent Agenda  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez

7.. New Transit Maintenance Facility Project Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 25-66 authorizing staff to proceed with the construction redesign plans to minimize the project footprint and lower costs, explore available grant funding opportunities and financing options to mitigate the City’s financial burden, and initiate a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the demolition of the former Commerce-Refuse-to-Energy Authority (CREA) site.
